project.title: IT support request (pilot candidate, pending confirmation)

sources.title: Verbal pilot brief (chat request, 23 September 2026)
sources.summary: The only input supplied for this discovery. Two candidate processes described in one sentence each; no procedure, export, volume or baseline record was supplied.

sections.title: Purchasing
sections.summary: Stated verbatim: takes 2 days; nobody will own it.

sections.title: IT support
sections.summary: Stated verbatim: takes 5 days; Ana owns it.

sections.title: Selection criterion offered by the requester
sections.summary: Stated verbatim: choose the fastest process for our pilot.

decisions.question: Confirm IT support as the pilot rather than purchasing. Purchasing is the shorter process (2 days against 5) but has no owner; a Provia workflow needs a named assignee on every action, so purchasing cannot be designed until someone owns it. Is the trade-off accepted?
decisions.owner: Pilot sponsor (not named in the brief)

decisions.question: Who owns purchasing end to end, and who approves a purchase? Until this is answered purchasing stays out of scope; if an owner appears, purchasing becomes the stronger second workflow.
decisions.owner: Pilot sponsor (not named in the brief)

decisions.question: Ana's full name, email and the scope of her ownership: does she own intake and triage, resolution, closure, or all of them? A single owner for every action is a design risk if she is also the only resolver.
Are '2 days' and '5 days' measured cycle times or estimates, and do they mean calendar days or workdays? No record was supplied, so neither figure can serve as a baseline yet.
decisions.owner: Pilot sponsor (not named in the brief)

decisions.question: How many IT support requests arrive per month, and through which channel today (email, telephone, in person)? The pilot needs enough real cases to learn from within the review window.

Which IT request types are in the pilot and which are excluded (for example: purchases of equipment, access requests, incidents affecting a whole site)? The proposed boundary is everyday requests that Ana's team resolves without a purchase.

Confirm country, jurisdiction, working language and currency for this project. Angola, pt-AO terminology, Africa/Luanda and AOA are the plugin's provisional starting context and were not stated by the requester; the manifest currently records language 'en' because the brief was written in English.
decisions.owner: Pilot sponsor (not named in the brief)
